slot.brief: Find the locus of z satisfying arg((z − α)/(z − β)) = π/2; derive the circle with α, β as endpoints of a diameter.

working:
Let $z=x+iy$. The real part of $(z+3-2i)\overline{(z-5-6i)}$ is $(x+3)(x-5)+(y-2)(y-6)$; setting it to zero gives $(x-1)^2+(y-4)^2=20$. Its imaginary part is $4(x-2y+7)$, which must be positive. Hence the locus is the stated open semicircle.

solution:
Let $z=x+iy$. Since the quotient has argument $\pi/2$, $(z+3-2i)\overline{(z-5-6i)}$ has zero real part and positive imaginary part:
$$ (x+3)(x-5)+(y-2)(y-6)=0 \implies (x-1)^2+(y-4)^2=20. $$
Its imaginary part is $4(x-2y+7)>0$, so the locus is $|z-(1+4i)|=2\sqrt5$ with $\operatorname{Re}z-2\operatorname{Im}z+7>0$.
